chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from his father, from Abi al-Bakhtari, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said:
"Whoever misses the Eid prayer, let him pray four [rak'at]."
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: And it does not contradict what we have said regarding the permissibility of praying individually, what has been narrated.
ai.seo_question: What should one do if they miss the Eid prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the specific legal ruling for an individual who misses the congregational Eid prayer, prescribing four units (rak'at) as the makeup. The accompanying commentary by al-Hilli clarifies that this individual performance does not contradict the general permissibility of praying alone, reinforcing the flexibility within Shia jurisprudence regarding communal versus private observance of Eid.
